nodes.title: How to Resample (img2img using an alternate modell)
widgets_values:
Load an image.

If you want to share the original positive and negative prompts, disable every optional stage, and see if a valid positive is generated by the image loaded node (if you see "beautiful scenery inside a glass bottle, purple galaxy, ...", that is a placeholder to share that the information is not available and it will be handled accordingly in the checking node). If you do not want the original prompt to be shared, simply link the empty "string" as the input for the "Original ... for Image Saver". Check the initial image's MP configuration.

Select the initial resize for the selected image (Opt Stage 0).
If enabling "Stage 3" (which has an Upscale and Resampler), I recommend a maximum of 4 MP. Otherwise up to 8 MP worked during my testing (and the amount of VRAM available on your system).

Note: progression in size: let's say your initial image is to 3 MP, Stage 1 and 2 will keep it at 3MP but stage 3 will increase it to 12MP with a 2x (3* 2x2 <- width and height doubling) and Stage 4 to 12 * 1.5x1.5 = 27MP. The multipliers for Stage 3 and 4 can be changed, but see above to decide on appropriate values to not run out of memory. 

After deciding which Resampler to enable, you can tweak the models and especially the denoise. The existing values are just the models I used and the locations of my models on disk, adapt as needed. Since this is a resampling step using an alternate mode, you can also influence the result with LoRAs (making sure to use model appropriate ones [Flux for Flux, ...]).

The Flux resampler makes use of ControlNets, we recommend a Tiled Depth one if a replacement is needed.

Krea2 tiled stages support random LoRA to restyle an image, if enabled.

Remember that a higher denoise means that more of the original image is going to be reinvented by the model.

This is also different from the using an image as an input for the "QwenVL Image to Prompt" combined with the "img2img" capabilities of the main workflow.

ComfyUI Manager: some nodes might not be resolved by default and might need to be installed from git directly.
1. https://github.com/lonecatone23/ComfyUI_LC123_nodes
2. https://github.com/lonecatone23/ComfyUI_LC_MaskMaker_nodes
3. https://github.com/Blakeem/ComfyUI-ContextAnchoredTileRefine

nodes.title: VRAM Control **attempts**
widgets_values:
Those bypassers serve as an extra option to attempt to release VRAM (using ComfyUI with an attention CLI parameter is recommended). Note that "yes" means "allow the node to run".
- `Clean VRAM` will **attempt** to release content from the VRAM. This is in addition to how ComfyUI performs its own caching.
- `VRAM Debug` will display the amount of VRAM available to be used. It will also **attempt** to release some as possible. The `Unload all models` below is another toggle available to **attempt** to free additional VRAM.

properties.lc_display_text:
sharp focus, crisp details, rich micro-texture, balanced lighting, accurate anatomy. A portrait shot from a strong upward perspective shows a cyberpunk woman in a powerful combat stance, holding two katana blades with iridescent blue and copper edges. She wears a modern denim kimono with a narrow geometric obi, leather belt, and short lace gloves, while a glowing orange cybernetic implant and a pulsing cybernetic eye cast light through thick sheets of rain. The scene is set beneath a towering corporate skyscraper with pulsating neon spires and golden holographic fish rippling across the sky, rendered as high contrast nocturnal cinematic film with intense starburst lens flares, chromatic aberration, vintage analog grain, rainbow light leaks, and ethereal glowing bloom.
